recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-5834 unless the work group later chooses a separate editorial rewrite of the cancelled definition outside this DSTU1 rename request.
issue_request: FHIR-5834 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core PA change request raised against DSTU1 EpisodeOfCare asking to rename EpisodeOfCare.currentStatus.withdrawn to cancelled, align descriptions and usage notes with other resources, and explain how withdrawn is represented.
initial_application: Git commit 8b7f2a91125c5387861132e44199814238044938 explicitly cited Tracker# 5206, 5833, 5834 and changed the EpisodeOfCare spreadsheet status list from withdrawn/other to finished/cancelled/waitlist, adding Cancelled wording that describes the withdrawn-from-service concept.
additional_context: The current resource no longer has currentStatus; source/fhir.ini actively includes episodeofcare=EpisodeOfCare, and the current status/statusHistory elements bind to the episode-of-care-status value set. The latest combined branch already lists cancelled in EpisodeOfCare.status and EpisodeOfCare.statusHistory.status and defines code cancelled in the Episode Of Care Status code system. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source has no withdrawn status code to rename, and the remaining phrase "withdrawn from service" appears only inside the cancelled code definition, which is consistent with the Jira resolution's instruction to describe how withdrawn is represented.

related_jiras.note: The same 2015 EpisodeOfCare reconciliation commit also handled the neighboring currentStatus.other issue, but this audit only decides FHIR-5834.
The same 2015 commit included a broader EpisodeOfCare ballot-comment tracker, but no independent decision for that issue was needed to reconcile FHIR-5834.
